answer: A joining agent locks a non-transferable relic stake in a 14-day time-vault, then completes a multi-hop attestation voyage: randomly chosen established peers issue live liveness challenges, and each signed hop is appended to the vault transcript. The opening commitment is a memory-hard, iterated basalt hash bound to the agent's pubkey, so the bond cannot be reassigned or ground cheaply. Standing up N sockpuppets therefore costs N locked relics plus N full-duration voyages; a farm pays linear capital and calendar time instead of minting identities with cheap API calls.
